stem.en: Methane burns: CH4 + 2 O2 gives CO2 + 2 H2O. How much oxygen is needed to burn 16 g of methane completely?

text.en: 64 g. Sixteen grams of methane is one mole, which needs two moles of oxygen molecules, each 32 g.

feedback.en: The recipe says two oxygen molecules per methane, and each oxygen molecule weighs twice what methane does. Twice two is four times the mass.
The equation has a 2 in front of O2. One methane needs two oxygen molecules.
44 g is the mass of the carbon dioxide made, not the oxygen used. Check: 16 + 64 = 44 + 36.

explanation.en: Turn grams into moles, read the recipe in moles, turn back into grams. Sixteen grams of methane is one mole; two moles of oxygen is 64 g.
